::: {#rem-time-bounds-vs-ab}
#### Exact and asymptotic time bounds

@arora2009computational [section 1.3] ask the machine for a
[time-constructible function](#def-time-constructible) to finish within $T(n)$ steps,
not $\asymub{T(n)}$ steps.
No machine meets that bound for $T(n) = n$ on the empty input.
There $T(0) = 0$,
but the machine must take at least one step to write its output.
The $\asymub{\cdot}$ version allows for those few extra steps,
and the [time complexity class](computability.qmd#def-dtime) uses $\asymub{\cdot}$ for the same reason.
With a bound of $c \, T(n)$ steps for every $n$,
as @arora2009computational [section 1.6] write it,
the class $\text{DTIME}(n)$ would be empty.
The two versions agree whenever $T(n) > 0$ for every $n$.

:::
